report.source_text: Currently, 20 months after the surgery, the patient feels good and does not report any alarming symptoms. Measurements of arterial tension and the heart rate carried out at home show normal results. Follow-up abdominal and thyroid ultrasonography is normal; isotopic analysis performed 8 months after the surgery (131- I MIBG scintigraphy) did not reveal any regions of abnormal accumulation of the tracer. The level of catecholamines and methoxycatecholamines in the control 24-h urine collection was normal (Table 1). Ophthalmic examinations showed significant regression of the changes described earlier. The patient’s vision has improved substantially and there are no signs of scotoma. Follow-up MRI of the CNS did not reveal abnormalities besides the presence of the arachnoid cyst. The lesions detected previously may have resulted from the developing encephalopathy. Slight muscular hyperthrophy of the left ventricle persists.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 14-year-old boy presented with bilateral scotoma, periodic headaches, dizziness, and severe arterial hypertension (180/98 mmHg, later 180/135 mmHg). Initial eye examination showed increased intraocular pressure and retinal detachment, attributed to hypertensive retinopathy (E002). A head CT revealed an arachnoid cyst and multiple brain foci (E001). Workup for suspected pheochromocytoma showed very high noradrenaline in blood serum and substantially elevated catecholamine and methoxycatecholamine levels in 24-hour urine (E008). An abdominal CT confirmed bilateral adrenal nodular lesions (right: 50x40x52 mm, left: 24 mm) (E009). Genetic testing identified a mutation in the VHL ex.1 p.Y112 C gene, confirming von Hippel-Lindau syndrome (E013). Following surgical intervention (implied), 20 months later, the patient reported feeling well with normal blood pressure and heart rate. Follow-up abdominal and thyroid ultrasonography were normal, and 131-I MIBG scintigraphy showed no abnormal tracer accumulation. Control 24-hour urine catecholamine levels were normal. Ophthalmic examinations showed significant regression of previous changes, improved vision, and no scotoma. Follow-up CNS MRI showed no abnormalities besides the arachnoid cyst, with previous brain foci attributed to encephalopathy (E014). Slight muscular hypertrophy of the left ventricle persisted (E014).
